books.title: Poorvi: Textbook of English for Grade 7

source.method: chapter titles from the book's Contents page; topics from each chapter PDF's section headings

topics.title: Reading the Story: Part I
objectives: Student can read Part I and describe Jahnavi's dream of going to school and why she was sad
Student can explain how the River begins to speak to Jahnavi
visualIdeas: a girl by a river with a kingfisher and a lizard
speech bubbles coming from the river

topics.title: Reading the Story: Part II
objectives: Student can explain the River's advice that "it's up to you" and how Jahnavi gathers courage to go to school
Student can describe how the teacher welcomes Jahnavi and what she wants to become
visualIdeas: a girl standing at a village school door holding her baby brother

topics.title: Thinking about the Story
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about the tone of the River and Jahnavi's feelings
Student can match Jahnavi's questions with the River's answers
visualIdeas: a two-column chart of Jahnavi's questions and the River's answers

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Sound Words, Borrowed Words and Prepositions
objectives: Student can explain why the author capitalises "River" when it is given human qualities
Student can use sound words from the text and find Indian-language origins of words like catamaran
Student can use prepositions and tell when words like up, down, on and off act as prepositions or adverbs
visualIdeas: word cards of sound words
a catamaran, a coracle and a shikara

topics.title: Listening and Speaking
objectives: Student can listen to five people speak about school life and match statements to speakers
Student can say a sentence in different voices and ask for and give advice in pairs
visualIdeas: five speaker icons with statements to match

topics.title: Writing: A Descriptive Paragraph about Nature
objectives: Student can write a titled descriptive paragraph about colours, shapes, textures and movements observed in nature
Student can use prompts like "Every day, I see..." and "I feel... as..." to express observations and feelings
visualIdeas: a notebook page of nature observations with sketches

topics.title: Reading the Poem
objectives: Student can read the poem aloud and retell how King Bruce learnt from a spider that kept trying
Student can explain the message of perseverance in the poem
visualIdeas: a spider climbing its thread while a king watches

topics.title: Thinking about the Poem
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about the King's despair and the spider's efforts
Student can complete a summary of the poem
visualIdeas: a timeline of the spider's attempts

topics.title: Words and Grammar: Opposites and Words of Effort and Distance
objectives: Student can write opposites of words from the poem and use words like toil, strive and endeavour in sentences
Student can classify words and phrases showing near and far distance
Student can say and make up tongue twisters
visualIdeas: a near/far sorting chart

topics.title: Listening and Speaking
objectives: Student can listen to a story about a determined ant and check predicted answers
Student can narrate a personal experience of being motivated not to give up
visualIdeas: an ant pulling a roti with other ants joining

topics.title: Writing: A Letter on Overcoming a Difficult Situation
objectives: Student can write a letter to a cousin sharing a plan to overcome a difficult situation, using transition words like "To begin with" and "Finally"
Student can use the format of an informal letter with address, date, greeting and closing
visualIdeas: a letter layout with address, date, greeting and closing

topics.title: Reading the Text
objectives: Student can read the text and explain how the writer, who cannot see, experiences the world through touch
Student can describe what the writer would like to see on each of the three days
visualIdeas: hands touching the bark of a tree and a leaf

topics.title: Thinking about the Text
objectives: Student can answer questions on extracts about the writer's feelings and tone
Student can identify true statements about the text
visualIdeas: a three-day plan drawn as a calendar

objectives: Student can collect sensory words for sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch

topics.title: Listening and Speaking
objectives: Student can listen to a conversation about Braille and assistive technology and mark statements true or false

topics.title: Writing: A Descriptive Paragraph about a Place
